last_judge_summary:
Not done. The full suite passes on team/authz (165 tests OK). The resolver-based matrix works: an unlisted URL fails, every role is tried with GET and POST, and records that don't exist or don't go together are tested. The admin redirect loop and the community_detail fixes are sound. Four major objections stand, all reproduced:
- C1/S3: merging team/compliance breaks 13 admin cells, so the builder's merge claim is false. The table also requires a permanent delete that skips README's 30-day evidence hold, and leaves that decision to Supreme against the owner's instruction.
- S1: the table marks 'yes' for a publisher outside a private group reading its member list, which the code comment and the doc say must not happen. The fix should only check private groups; the challenger's version, which checks every audience, would break unit news.
- S2: a moderator can re-attribute a post and make a private group's post company-wide in the admin.
- C3: the module-level TEMP_MEDIA is shared by two classes, so CI's forked --parallel 4 run on Linux can fail depending on timing.
Also upheld: C2 (the doc claims moderators open hidden and deleted posts; they get 404), C4 (staff status, which org admins and Communications will have, also grants all-staff announcements, and this is neither tested nor written down) and C5 (minor: 'yes' overclaims that the action was done). Rejected as minor or out of scope: C6, C7, C8, S4, S5, S6. Remaining minor follow-ups: a content-marker check on 'yes' pages, org admins joining private groups without anyone being told, and moderators commenting or voting in private groups. The Netlify board part of the user's request belongs to a separate workflow step; this judge did not touch Netlify. The worktree C:/Users/rzvm_/.worktrees/authz-judge-r1 has been removed. Not checked here: Linux fork behaviour (checked by reading Django's runner), real single sign-on, Postgres and Docker.

last_build.summary:
All seven required fixes are done in one commit, 5a6c120, on team/authz. The full suite passes (167 tests OK). Merging with team/compliance and team/redteam is clean. With compliance merged, the matrix agrees with compliance's admin: only the new privacy_notice address needs a row. Merging with team/rollout still conflicts in hub/admin.py, in exactly the lines where compliance and rollout already conflict with each other. Docker, Postgres and real single sign-on were not available, so they were not checked.

What changed:
- Admin delete: posts, comments and reports have no Delete page, for the superuser too. The code is team/compliance's exact lines.
- Moderators can no longer change a post's or comment's author, group, words or date in the admin.
- The must-read readers list now gives "not found" if the news went to a private group the person can't see. Units are left out.
- The publisher and the org admin now have staff status in the test, as Supreme will set them up. A test checks that staff status alone gives the Announcement tick.
- Each test class gets its own media folder, so CI's parallel workers can't delete each other's files.
- docs/security/ACCESS-MATRIX.md matches all of this.

The rollout conflict needs one hand decision: compliance's "Delete selected (removed for good after 30 days)" action and rollout's "Delete selected again" do the same job.
open_items: Merging team/compliance: the matrix then fails only because the new privacy_notice address has no row. Whoever merges adds one row in 'Before signing in' (yes for signed out, leaver and new starter) and one in 'Alerts, settings, search and about' (yes for all eight columns). This was measured. The 13 admin cells no longer break.

Merging team/rollout conflicts in hub/admin.py in the same two places where compliance and rollout already conflict with each other. My own lines merge cleanly. Rollout's delete_again action uses permissions=['delete'], and compliance's has_delete_permission(obj=None) returns False, so that action never shows. A trial merge resolved to my side fails rollout's test_items_kept_for_a_closed_case_are_deleted_again_and_purged_after_30_days. The merger must decide: keep compliance's delete_later and point rollout's test at it, or give delete_again permissions=['soft_delete'].

Merging team/qa changes 12 matrix cells. QA's event_edit and event_delete now answer 'hidden' instead of 'refused' to the colleague, publisher, editor and moderator, who can't see the event. QA's change depends on kept_for_report, so copying it was not practical. The merger updates those 12 cells and drops the 'Deleting someone else's post, comment or event' note for events.

Merging team/reliability adds the /healthz address, which needs a row in both tables (measured: 3 matrix tests fail until it has one). The hardening, experience, foundations, handover and redteam trial merges keep the matrix green. The redteam merge also passes all its security tests and tests_features (86 tests OK).
If team/compliance changes its admin.py lines again, my copy of them will conflict at the next merge.

Side effect, recorded as decided: deleting a group, person or event in the admin removes its posts and comments at once, skipping the 30-day keep, unless an open report holds one. Only the superuser can do this.
Minor follow-ups the judge left open: checking page content on 'yes' cells, org admins joining private groups without anyone being told, and moderators commenting or voting in private groups.
Not checked here: CI's forked --parallel 4 on Linux (this PC runs Windows), Postgres, Docker, real Entra ID single sign-on, and manage.py check --deploy with production settings.
